2.v:
This sheet holds the randomly generated standard normal variables (epsilon). 
1. Adjust the number of days in row 8 to match the number of work days to expiration for the option. 
2. Go to 'Data/Data Analysis/Random Number Generation'. Set the number of variables equal to teh number of working days to expiration. Set the number of variables equal to 1000. Set the distribution to Normal(0,1). Set the output range to the highlighted range in this sheet.

body.dataStream: This sheet holds the simulated log stock prices, computed using the randomly generated epsilons and the formula for the log stock price given in the case study. 1. Adjust the number of days in row 8 to match the number of work days to expiration for the option. 2. The day zero log price is equal to the natural logarithm of the current stock price for all simulations. 3. The stock price from day 1 onwards is computed using the dynamic formula given in the case study, referencing the previous day's log stock price and the current day's epsilon.

This sheet holds the simulated log stock prices, computed using the randomly generated epsilons and the formula for the log stock price given in the case study. 
1. Adjust the number of days in row 8 to match the number of work days to expiration for the option. 
2. The day zero log price is equal to the natural logarithm of the current stock price for all simulations. 
3. The stock price from day 1 onwards is computed using the dynamic formula given in the case study, referencing the previous day's log stock price and the current day's epsilon.
